summary: Several added comments overstate behavior or omit an inherited failure guarantee.

items.issue: The documentation omits the material case where `remappingFunction` throws. The inherited contract states that the exception is propagated and no update is made; this implementation likewise calls the function before entering any update case.
items.suggestion: State that an exception thrown by `remappingFunction` is propagated and the method makes no update.

items.issue: It does not populate counters for every table block as documented. `totalSizeMapBuckets` is zero for tables shorter than 32 and one for every table longer than 32, so the loop skips all entries or counts only the first 32 buckets.
items.suggestion: Do not claim that every block is rebuilt unless the implementation is fixed; otherwise document its actual limited behavior.

items.issue: The comment promises a positive power of two at least as large as any `target`, but targets above `1 << 30` produce `Int.MinValue` because of the shift, rather than a positive result.
items.suggestion: Document the supported input range and overflow behavior, or fix the implementation to reject/handle oversized targets.

items.issue: The returned value is the exact `elems` reference. `C` is constrained only to `IterableOnce`, and subclasses can mutate that object rather than replace it, so later additions are not universally unable to affect an earlier result.
items.suggestion: Qualify the guarantee as depending on subclasses maintaining the immutable/replacement invariant, or enforce that invariant.

bonus_findings.issue: The block-count condition appears reversed: tables below 32 yield zero blocks, while tables above 32 always yield one.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Use one block for tables shorter than `sizeMapBucketSize` and otherwise divide the table length by that size.
